The pinned latest admitted source-path alias wins; ordinary content-addressed aliases require matching length/hash. Distinct aliases remain distinct. Rejected admissions preserve caller custody, previous input state and subsequent stream ordinals.

Sealed manifests retain only name/path/length/hash fields and bound path and descriptor-text sizes. Assembly admission separately limits input count, retained descriptor count/text, summed input-entry bytes and the deduplicated final ZIP.

Sealing transfers custody once. Builder disposal cannot delete transferred files. Final archive disposal waits for its active reader, releases every input reader before cleanup, uses four cleanup workers, settles all owners and preserves the earliest input cleanup failure.

Actual browser chunks retain snapshots, filmstrips, sources and original response bytes after context/browser closure. The six composite archives load in the pinned loader and match their three original input archives byte-for-byte with declared naming/alias selection.
